note: Single source for the camera library. docs/CAMERA_MOVEMENTS.md is generated from this file (python scripts/catana.py docs). Speeds: slow | medium | fast. min_seconds = shortest clip in which the move reads cleanly.

movements.name: Static (locked-off)
movements.definition: The camera does not move; all motion comes from the subject or the scene.
best_for: letting a performance or action carry the shot
movements.camera_behavior: Fixed position, fixed framing, no drift, no zoom.
movements.subject_behavior: Provides all the motion: gestures, walking through frame, liquids, fabric, light changes.
movements.prompt_phrase: locked-off static camera on a tripod, no camera movement
movements.example_prompt: Locked-off static camera on a tripod, medium shot of a barista pouring latte art, steam curling up, warm window light from camera left.
common_mistakes: asking for a static camera and a camera move in the same prompt
static shots with no subject motion read as frozen stills

movements.name: Dolly In
movements.definition: The whole camera travels forward on a track toward the subject; perspective and parallax change as distance closes.
movements.camera_behavior: Smooth constant-speed forward travel at fixed height, lens unchanged; background shifts with real parallax.
movements.subject_behavior: Usually holds position or makes one small action so the move does the storytelling.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} dolly in toward the subject on a smooth track, constant height, real parallax in the background
movements.example_prompt: Slow dolly in toward a matte-black wristwatch on a basalt plinth, constant height, softbox key from the left, background studio haze drifting with parallax.
common_mistakes: calling a zoom a dolly (a zoom has no parallax)
combining with dolly out or pull out
too fast for a short clip so the subject blows past the frame

movements.name: Dolly Out
movements.definition: The camera travels backward away from the subject on a track, widening the frame and revealing surroundings with parallax.
best_for: showing a product in its environment
movements.camera_behavior: Smooth constant-speed backward travel at fixed height; foreground elements may enter frame edges.
movements.subject_behavior: Holds or recedes in relative size; the environment becomes the story.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} dolly out away from the subject, revealing the surrounding space with natural parallax
movements.example_prompt: Slow dolly out from a woman standing at a floor-to-ceiling window at blue hour, revealing the empty penthouse living room around her.
common_mistakes: combining with dolly in
revealing nothing new: the wider frame must add information

movements.name: Push In
movements.definition: A slow, subtle forward creep, smaller than a dolly in, used to build tension or intimacy.
movements.camera_behavior: Very slow forward movement, barely perceptible, ending a little tighter than it started.
movements.subject_behavior: Minimal: a breath, a glance, a slight turn of the head.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} subtle push in, barely perceptible forward creep
movements.example_prompt: Subtle slow push in on the face of an elderly fisherman as he looks out to sea, overcast soft light, shallow depth of field.
common_mistakes: making it fast (then it is a dolly in)
pairing with large subject motion that hides the move

movements.name: Pull Out
movements.definition: The camera eases backward from a detail to a wider view, often ending on a reveal.
movements.camera_behavior: Starts tight on a detail and eases back; speed may ramp slightly at the start or end.
movements.subject_behavior: The detail stays readable as it becomes part of the larger picture.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} pull out from a close detail to a wide reveal
movements.example_prompt: Slow pull out from a macro of hand-stitched leather to reveal the full handbag on a travertine counter in a sunlit boutique.
common_mistakes: starting too wide so nothing is revealed
combining with a push in

movements.name: Tracking Shot
movements.definition: The camera travels alongside, ahead of or behind a moving subject, keeping pace with it.
best_for: following a character through a space
movements.camera_behavior: Matches the subject's speed and direction, keeping framing consistent; background streams past.
movements.subject_behavior: Moves continuously in one clear direction.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} tracking shot moving alongside the subject at matching speed, background streaming past
movements.example_prompt: Side tracking shot moving alongside a model walking down a sunlit concrete colonnade, camera matching her pace, shadows of columns sliding across her.
common_mistakes: a static subject (nothing to track)
changing the subject's direction mid-shot
mixing with orbit

movements.name: Orbit 360
movements.definition: The camera circles the subject a full 360 degrees at constant distance and height, keeping it centred.
best_for: showing a building from every side
movements.camera_behavior: Constant radius and height, smooth angular speed, subject locked in centre frame.
movements.subject_behavior: Mostly stationary so the orbit reads; small idle motion is fine.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} 360-degree orbit around the subject at constant distance and height, subject held in centre frame
movements.example_prompt: Smooth 360-degree orbit around a ceramic perfume bottle on a mirrored plinth, constant distance, soft gradient backdrop, caustic reflections sweeping across the glass.
common_mistakes: clips under ~6 s (a full orbit becomes a blur)
moving subjects that drift off-centre
the back of the subject never designed (models invent geometry)

movements.name: Arc Shot
movements.definition: A partial orbit (roughly 30–180 degrees) around the subject, changing the viewing angle with a sense of reveal.
movements.camera_behavior: Curved path at constant distance, typically 45–120 degrees; may finish with a slight push.
movements.subject_behavior: Holds a pose or turns slightly against the arc for energy.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} arc shot, camera curving about 90 degrees around the subject at constant distance
movements.example_prompt: Slow arc shot curving 90 degrees around a boxer taping his hands in a dim locker room, single overhead tungsten bulb, dust in the light.
common_mistakes: not stating the angle (models over-rotate)
combining with a full orbit

movements.name: Crane Up
movements.definition: The camera rises on a crane or jib arm, usually tilting down to keep the subject in frame, opening up the space.
movements.camera_behavior: Rises smoothly in an arc, often with a compensating tilt down.
movements.subject_behavior: Becomes smaller in frame as the environment opens.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} crane up, camera rising on a jib while tilting down to keep the subject framed
movements.example_prompt: Slow crane up from a couple at a candlelit table on a rooftop terrace, rising to reveal the city skyline at dusk.
common_mistakes: confusing with tilt up (a tilt does not change height)
combining with crane down

movements.name: Crane Down
movements.definition: The camera descends on a crane or jib, moving from an overview into the scene.
best_for: openings that land on a character
movements.camera_behavior: Descends smoothly, often tilting up to stay on the subject.
movements.subject_behavior: Grows in frame; often begins an action as the camera lands.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} crane down from a high vantage point, descending into the scene and settling on the subject
movements.example_prompt: Slow crane down from above a desert courtyard, descending past palm fronds to settle on a woman opening a carved wooden door.
common_mistakes: landing on nothing in particular
combining with crane up

movements.name: Pedestal Movement
movements.definition: The camera moves straight up or down without tilting, keeping the lens level; framing slides vertically.
best_for: revealing tall products or façades level-on
scanning a figure head to toe
movements.camera_behavior: Pure vertical translation, lens stays level, verticals stay parallel.
movements.subject_behavior: Static; the framing slides along it.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} pedestal {direction}, camera rising straight vertically with the lens kept level, no tilt
movements.example_prompt: Slow pedestal up along the façade of a white stone villa, lens kept level, verticals perfectly parallel, midday shadows under each balcony.
common_mistakes: models add a tilt unless 'no tilt' and 'lens level' are stated
combining with crane in the same direction

movements.name: Tilt Up
movements.definition: The camera pivots upward on a fixed point, revealing what is above.
best_for: ending on a sky or logo
movements.camera_behavior: Fixed position, rotates upward around the horizontal axis.
movements.subject_behavior: Usually static so the reveal reads.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} tilt up from the base to the top, camera position fixed
movements.example_prompt: Slow tilt up from the marble entrance steps to the top of a glass tower against a cloudless sky.
common_mistakes: calling it 'pan up'
verticals converge on buildings: if geometry must stay straight use pedestal

movements.name: Tilt Down
movements.definition: The camera pivots downward on a fixed point, moving from sky or high detail to the subject.
movements.camera_behavior: Fixed position, rotates downward around the horizontal axis.
movements.subject_behavior: Revealed at the end of the move.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} tilt down from the sky to reveal the subject, camera position fixed
movements.example_prompt: Slow tilt down from swaying palm crowns to a turquoise infinity pool where a swimmer surfaces.
common_mistakes: combining with tilt up
starting on empty sky for too long in a short clip

movements.name: Pan Left
movements.definition: The camera rotates horizontally to the left from a fixed position.
movements.camera_behavior: Fixed position, rotates left around the vertical axis at even speed.
movements.subject_behavior: Moves left or is revealed by the pan.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} pan left across the scene, camera position fixed
movements.example_prompt: Slow pan left across a misty tea plantation at sunrise, pickers moving between the rows.
common_mistakes: combining pan left and pan right
fast pans judder: use whip pan or slow down

movements.name: Pan Right
movements.definition: The camera rotates horizontally to the right from a fixed position.
movements.camera_behavior: Fixed position, rotates right around the vertical axis at even speed.
movements.subject_behavior: Moves right or is revealed by the pan.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} pan right across the scene, camera position fixed
movements.example_prompt: Slow pan right along a sunlit kitchen island to reveal a family laughing at the breakfast table.
common_mistakes: combining pan right and pan left
too fast for the clip length

movements.name: Whip Pan
movements.definition: An extremely fast pan that blurs the frame, used as an energetic transition between moments.
movements.camera_behavior: Snaps horizontally in a fraction of a second with heavy motion blur, settling on a new framing.
movements.subject_behavior: Before and after the whip, subjects are clearly framed; during it everything streaks.
movements.prompt_phrase: sudden whip pan with heavy motion blur, snapping to a new framing
movements.example_prompt: Medium shot of a chef plating a dish, then a sudden whip pan with heavy motion blur snapping to the diner taking the first bite.
common_mistakes: using it inside slow luxury pieces
asking for it with a slow push in
no clear frame to land on

movements.name: Zoom In
movements.definition: The focal length lengthens so the frame tightens without the camera moving; no parallax change.
movements.camera_behavior: Camera fixed, field of view narrows, background compresses.
movements.subject_behavior: Grows in frame with flat perspective.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} optical zoom in, camera position fixed, background compressing
movements.example_prompt: Slow optical zoom in on a lone lighthouse on a cliff in a storm, camera fixed, 1970s documentary look.
common_mistakes: asking for a 'zoom' when you want a dolly's parallax
combining zoom in and dolly out without saying 'dolly zoom'

movements.name: Zoom Out
movements.definition: The focal length shortens so the frame widens without the camera moving.
movements.camera_behavior: Camera fixed, field of view widens, perspective stays flat.
movements.subject_behavior: Shrinks in frame as context appears.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} optical zoom out, camera position fixed, revealing the wider scene
movements.example_prompt: Slow optical zoom out from a hiker on a ridge to reveal the vast glacier valley below.
common_mistakes: expecting parallax (use dolly out)
combining with zoom in

movements.name: FPV Drone
movements.definition: A fast, agile first-person-view drone flight that dives, banks and threads through gaps.
movements.camera_behavior: Fast forward flight with banking rolls, dives and close passes; slight wide-angle distortion.
movements.subject_behavior: Environment rushes past; people stay small or are passed by.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} FPV drone flight, diving and banking, threading close through the space with wide-angle lens
movements.example_prompt: Fast FPV drone flight diving from the sky over a modern villa, banking through the open living room doors, skimming the pool surface and rising over the palm garden.
common_mistakes: too many waypoints for the clip length
using it where calm and luxury is the brief
combining with a locked-off tripod

movements.name: Aerial Reveal
movements.definition: A smooth drone move (rising, pulling back or flying over an obstacle) that reveals a location at scale.
movements.camera_behavior: Slow, stable aerial travel; often starts behind a foreground element and rises or glides past it.
movements.subject_behavior: The location is the subject; small figures or vehicles give scale.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} aerial drone reveal, gliding up and over the foreground to reveal the location at scale
movements.example_prompt: Slow aerial drone reveal rising over a dune ridge to reveal a contemporary desert resort glowing at golden hour.
common_mistakes: no foreground element to reveal from
too fast (reads as FPV)

movements.name: Top-Down
movements.definition: The camera looks straight down at 90 degrees, flattening the scene into a graphic plan.
movements.camera_behavior: Lens pointing straight down; may drift, rotate slowly or rise straight up.
movements.subject_behavior: Reads as shapes and patterns; motion across the frame is strongest.
movements.prompt_phrase: top-down overhead view, camera pointing straight down at 90 degrees, {speed} slow rotation
movements.example_prompt: Top-down overhead view of a breakfast flat lay on a linen tablecloth, camera pointing straight down, hands entering frame to pour coffee.
common_mistakes: also asking for eye-level framing
tracking or orbit moves that break the straight-down axis

movements.name: Handheld
movements.definition: The camera is held by an operator, with natural micro-shake and reactive reframing.
movements.camera_behavior: Small organic shake, breathing drift, reactive reframes; never mechanical.
movements.subject_behavior: Natural, unposed behaviour; the camera reacts to it.
movements.prompt_phrase: handheld camera with subtle natural shake and organic reframing
movements.example_prompt: Handheld camera with subtle natural shake following a young woman unboxing sneakers on her bedroom floor, daylight from a window, phone-camera realism.
common_mistakes: combining with steadicam, gimbal or locked-off
exaggerated shake that makes viewers ill

movements.name: Steadicam
movements.definition: A stabilised, floating camera that moves freely through space with fluid motion.
movements.camera_behavior: Smooth, floating travel with gentle curves; no shake, no track lines.
movements.subject_behavior: Leads the camera through the space or is circled gently.
movements.prompt_phrase: smooth steadicam move, floating stabilised camera gliding through the space
movements.example_prompt: Smooth steadicam move gliding from the entrance hall into a double-height living room, following a host who gestures toward the garden view.
common_mistakes: combining with handheld
using it for a locked composition

movements.name: Bullet Time
movements.definition: Time freezes or slows to near-zero while the camera keeps moving around the subject.
movements.camera_behavior: Arcs around the subject at normal speed while the scene is frozen or ultra-slow.
movements.subject_behavior: Frozen mid-action: droplets, debris and hair suspended in the air.
movements.prompt_phrase: bullet time: the action frozen in mid-air while the camera arcs {speed} around the subject
movements.example_prompt: Bullet time: a sneaker frozen mid-splash in a puddle, droplets suspended in the air, the camera arcing slowly around it, neon reflections.
common_mistakes: subject still moving at normal speed
clips shorter than 3 s
too many frozen elements for the model to keep stable

movements.name: Dutch Angle
movements.definition: The camera is rolled on its axis so the horizon is tilted, creating unease or energy.
movements.camera_behavior: Rolled 10–30 degrees; can be static or combined with a move.
movements.subject_behavior: Any; the tilt reframes it.
movements.prompt_phrase: dutch angle, camera rolled about 20 degrees so the horizon tilts
movements.example_prompt: Dutch angle, camera rolled 20 degrees, a detective in a rain-soaked alley under a flickering neon sign.
common_mistakes: using it on architecture that must look straight
rolling so far it reads as an error

movements.name: Rack Focus
movements.definition: Focus shifts from one plane to another within the shot, redirecting attention.
movements.camera_behavior: Usually static or slow-moving; shallow depth of field; focus transitions smoothly between planes.
movements.subject_behavior: Two clear subjects at different depths.
movements.prompt_phrase: rack focus from the {from} in the foreground to the {to} in the background, shallow depth of field
movements.example_prompt: Static shot, rack focus from raindrops on a café window in the foreground to a woman reading inside, shallow depth of field, 85mm.
common_mistakes: deep depth of field (nothing to rack)
only one subject plane
not naming both focus targets

movements.name: Parallax Movement
movements.definition: A lateral or diagonal move past layered foreground, midground and background so depth separates visibly.
best_for: showing depth in interiors and landscapes
movements.camera_behavior: Slow sideways slide; near objects move faster than far ones.
movements.subject_behavior: Static or slow; the depth layers do the work.
movements.prompt_phrase: {speed} lateral parallax slide past layered foreground elements, strong depth separation
movements.example_prompt: Slow lateral parallax slide past blurred olive branches in the foreground, revealing a white villa terrace in the midground and the sea beyond.
common_mistakes: no foreground layer (no parallax to see)
combining with a locked-off camera
